title: Economists
description: Conduct research, prepare reports, or formulate plans to address economic problems related to the production and distribution of goods and services or monetary and fiscal policy. May collect and process economic and statistical data using sampling techniques and econometric methods.

tasks.text: Study the socioeconomic impacts of new public policies, such as proposed legislation, taxes, services, and regulations.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Provide advice and consultation on economic relationships to businesses, public and private agencies, and other employers.
Formulate recommendations, policies, or plans to solve economic problems or to interpret markets.
Compile, analyze, and report data to explain economic phenomena and forecast market trends, applying mathematical models and statistical techniques.
Forecast production and consumption of renewable resources and supply, consumption, and depletion of non-renewable resources.
Conduct research on economic issues, and disseminate research findings through technical reports or scientific articles in journals.
Provide litigation support, such as writing reports for expert testimony or testifying as an expert witness.
Study economic and statistical data in area of specialization, such as finance, labor, or agriculture.

clusters.label: Interpreting the Meaning of Information for Others

tasks.text: Explain economic impact of policies to the public.
Supervise research projects and students' study projects.
Develop economic guidelines and standards, and prepare points of view used in forecasting trends and formulating economic policy.
Teach theories, principles, and methods of economics.
Testify at regulatory or legislative hearings concerning the estimated effects of changes in legislation or public policy, and present recommendations based on cost-benefit analyses.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Operations Analysis
skills.def: Analyzing needs and product requirements to create a design.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: Aptech Systems GAUSS, Camfit Data Limited Microfit, Econometric Software LIMDEP, Estima Regression Analysis of Time Series RATS.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C++, Microsoft Visual C# .NET, Oracle Java, Python.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Microsoft Access, Microsoft SQL Server, Structured query language SQL.

skills.name: Business intelligence and data analysis software
skills.def: Software to present, visualize, or analyze data to help businesses make informed decisions. Examples: Microsoft Power BI, Tableau.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Corel QuattroPro, IBM Lotus 1-2-3, Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Corel WordPerfect Office Suite, Microsoft Office software.
